instances.scenario: An attacker submits feedback through the unauthenticated feedback API with a script-bearing comment. The About page wraps the comment in markup, marks it trusted HTML and renders it with innerHTML for every visitor, so the script runs and can read the JWT in localStorage.

An attacker registers an account whose email contains an HTML payload. The administration page wraps each email in a span, marks it trusted HTML and renders it with innerHTML, so the payload runs when an administrator opens the page.
An attacker posts feedback containing an HTML payload. The administration page marks each comment as trusted HTML and renders it with innerHTML, so the payload runs in the administrator's browser.

The last-login-IP view decodes the JWT from localStorage and passes data.lastLoginIp to the Angular sanitizer bypass as an HTML string. If an attacker gets markup into that claim, for example through a forged client-IP header recorded at login, it runs script in the victim's session and can read the localStorage token.

The last-login-ip page decodes the stored JWT and wraps data.lastLoginIp in HTML marked as trusted, then binds it via innerHTML. If an attacker can set the recorded login IP (for example through a client-supplied header stored by the server), script runs in the victim's origin on the next visit and can steal the JWT from localStorage.

The search page reads the q query parameter, marks it as trusted HTML with the sanitizer bypass, and binds it to innerHTML. An attacker sends a victim a crafted search link; script runs in the shop origin and can read the JWT from localStorage.
